editorial:
Imagine moving into a new house only to find out that the previous owner didn't really leave. You will follow a young couple who just bought a place that seems perfect, but things get creepy fast. The vibe is very chilly and slow, making you feel like something is watching you from the corners of the room. It doesn't rely on loud noises to scare you; instead, it builds a feeling of dread that stays with you long after the scene ends. You will feel the tension grow as the main characters realize they are not alone in their own home.

The acting is solid and makes the fear feel real. While the story moves a bit slow at times, the payoff is worth the wait. If you like ghosts and mysteries, you will love this. It is a great pick for a rainy night.
endingExplained: You find out that the ghost is a woman who was murdered in the house. She is not just random; she is tied to a dark secret involving the property. In the final scenes, the truth about her death comes out through a series of shocks. The movie wraps up by showing that some spirits cannot be calmed down easily. You see that the horror follows the characters even when they try to escape the house.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow-burn Japanese ghost stories.
